headline: An AI tool that estimates whether early breast cancer will come back has won FDA clearance and can give the estimate before surgery.
score_reason: Cleared clinical tool with real study numbers; no outside review of the company's data reported.
importance_line: Women with the most common type of early breast cancer and their doctors get a recurrence estimate before surgery, but the evidence so far is a review of past records and insurers have not yet agreed to cover it.
summary: ABC News reports that the FDA has cleared TumorSight Risk, made by SimBioSys and powered by NVIDIA chips, which reads a patient's existing breast MRI together with pathology results to score her chance of cancer returning within five to ten years. In a study of 2,129 women, 95.5% of those rated low risk stayed cancer-free after five years against 89.6% of those rated high risk, and SimBioSys says it is working with Medicare, Medicaid and private insurers to get the test covered.
notes: Retrospective study; the figures come from the company's analysis as relayed by ABC News. Applies to hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative early-stage cancer.
